title: Scripture and Preaching
definition: Scripture and preaching belong together because biblical preaching declares, explains, applies, and exalts the Word of God.
summary: Preaching is not the display of human opinion but the faithful proclamation of God's truth for conviction, comfort, correction, and discipleship.
christFocus: Christ is proclaimed through Scripture-centered preaching as Savior, Lord, and hope.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture and Preaching teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to scripture and preaching by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
